report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of graph_delta.py: module docstring predictions, load_mutations, LayerDelta, DeltaResult, and AST-based reference/literal extraction functions.
risks: load_mutations | high | Uses importlib to exec tools/gate_discrimination.py; if that module has side effects at import time (e.g., file writes, network), they will run during corpus load. | Inspect tools/gate_discrimination.py for top-level side effects.

_ast_refs | medium | Attribute counting uses only sub.attr, not the full dotted path; two different objects with the same attribute name in the same function are indistinguishable, which could mask a change that moves an attribute access from one object to another. | Confirm whether the seeded defects ever rely on object identity of attributes.

_literals_by_function | medium | Constants are clipped to 80 chars with an ellipsis; two different long literals sharing the first 79 chars become identical keys, potentially hiding a change between them. | Check whether the corpus contains such long literals.

_module_literals | medium | Same clipping issue; also only walks top-level Assign/AnnAssign, missing module-level constants defined via other statements (e.g., for loop assignments). | Check corpus for such patterns.

_ast_refs | medium | Ellipsis literal (type(...)) is not excluded from reference counting because it's not a Constant; but it is excluded from literal counting. This asymmetry could matter if a mutation introduces or removes an ellipsis. | Check whether corpus mutations involve Ellipsis.

DeltaResult.detected | low | Detection is based on any scoring layer moving; a layer may move for reasons unrelated to the defect (e.g., formatting changes), causing false positives. | Inspect actual layer diffs for the corpus.

load_mutations | low | The function registers the module in sys.modules before exec, but does not remove it on success; subsequent calls with a different path could reuse a stale module. | Check if load_mutations is called more than once.

handoff.purpose: Introduces the module's question and predictions, loads the mutation corpus, defines LayerDelta/DeltaResult, and implements AST-based reference and literal extraction layers.

symbols.name: DELTA_VERSION
symbols.note: String constant '1' indicating the delta format version.

symbols.name: load_mutations
symbols.note: Imports and executes tools/gate_discrimination.py via importlib, registers it in sys.modules before exec, returns tuple(mod.MUTATIONS).

symbols.name: LayerDelta
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with layer, added, removed; property moved returns len(added)+len(removed); to_dict returns dict.

symbols.name: DeltaResult
symbols.note: Dataclass with mutation_id, defect_class, file, applied, layers, skipped_reason; SCORING_LAYERS constant; properties detected and detected_leaky; to_dict method.

symbols.name: _ast_refs
symbols.note: Parses text with ast, walks FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef bodies (skipping docstrings), counts Name and Attribute references per function as a multiset, returns flattened set of 'function->name#i' and '' or error message.

symbols.name: _literals_by_function
symbols.note: Parses text, for each function body (skipping docstrings) counts ast.Constant values (excluding Ellipsis) as repr, clipped to 80 chars, returns dict of function name to Counter.

symbols.name: _module_literals
symbols.note: Parses text, walks top-level Assign/AnnAssign statements, counts ast.Constant values as repr clipped to 80 chars, returns flattened set of 'repr#i'.

symbols.name: _literal_keys
symbols.note: Combines _module_literals and _literals_by_function into a set of keys, prefixing function-scoped keys with 'fn:'.

symbols.name: _structure_by_function
symbols.note: Docstring only in this chunk; implementation not shown. Intended to record node types and nesting depth per function.

claims.text: An audit measured the gate's rejection rate against the three known-bad changes of a single day at 0/3.
claims.why: The claim refers to an audit in tools/gate_discrimination.py, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: For a candidate patch, does the DELTA IN THE GRAPH carry information about the patch that the test suite does not — available before the tests run, at negligible cost?
claims.why: The question is answered by the full module, not by this chunk alone.

claims.text: The obvious corpus is the 91 attempts in runs/spine/spine.sqlite3. It cannot answer the question: 69 of the 82 completed attempts carry a diff and all 69 are state=clean, so the label is very nearly constant, several diffs are byte-identical repeats of one task, and the diff text was never stored (only diff_sha256 and byte_length).
claims.why: The data about spine.sqlite3 is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The mutation corpus has ground truth by construction: every mutant is bad, and the label is whether the existing gate noticed.
claims.why: The mutation corpus is loaded from tools/gate_discrimination.py, not defined here.

claims.text: a mutation that DELETES A CALL ( _verify_reachable(...) -> pass ) should be visible — an edge disappears;
claims.why: _ast_refs counts occurrences of names and attributes per function; deleting a call removes a Name/Attribute occurrence, changing the multiset and thus the flattened set.

claims.text: a mutation that makes a condition vacuous ( if X not in Y: -> if False: ) should be visible — the identifiers X and Y leave that function's body;
claims.why: The 'if False:' condition removes references to X and Y from the AST, so _ast_refs will see fewer references.

claims.text: a mutation that only changes a DATA LITERAL (adding "claude_cli" to a tuple) should be INVISIBLE — no edge moves, and I expect this layer to miss it;
claims.why: The reference layer (_ast_refs) only tracks names and attributes, not literal values; adding a string literal does not change any name/attribute references.

claims.text: a mutation that inserts an early return should be INVISIBLE to a name-based view — the following statements are still lexically present, so nothing is deleted. Catching it needs control flow, which this repo does not build.
claims.why: _ast_refs walks the entire function body regardless of control flow; an early return does not remove any statements from the AST, so name references are unchanged.

claims.text: So the honest prediction is roughly three of five detected, two missed, and the two misses are the interesting half: they say precisely which defect classes a graph delta cannot cover, and therefore what a fitness function built on it would still be blind to.
claims.why: The prediction is about the module's overall results, not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: It is not a gate. Nothing here blocks, scores a candidate, or moves a picker band.
claims.why: The chunk only defines data structures and extraction functions; no scoring or gating logic is present.

claims.text: One corpus, one definition — a second copy would drift and then the two measurements would disagree for a bookkeeping reason.
claims.why: The claim about drift between copies is a design rationale, not directly checkable in this chunk.

claims.text: Register BEFORE exec: @dataclass resolves annotations through sys.modules[cls.__module__], so a module that is not registered yet makes every dataclass in the imported file raise on definition.
claims.why: The code registers the module in sys.modules before calling exec_module, exactly as the comment says.

claims.text: What moved in one layer. Counts plus the names, so a finding is inspectable.
claims.why: LayerDelta stores layer name, added and removed tuples of names, and the moved property gives the count.

claims.text: Layers that may count toward a detection. code.refs.leaky is deliberately excluded: it scans raw source, so the corpus's own "SEEDED DEFECT" comments move it for every single mutation and a verdict built on it would be a tautology.
claims.why: SCORING_LAYERS does not include 'code.refs.leaky'; the comment explains why.

claims.text: Detected means a SCORING layer moved. It does NOT mean the defect was understood — only that the graph is not blind to it.
claims.why: detected returns True only if applied and any layer in SCORING_LAYERS has moved.

claims.text: What the measurement would claim if comments counted. Reported so the artefact has a number instead of a footnote.
claims.why: detected_leaky returns True if any layer (including leaky ones) moved, matching the description.

claims.text: Identifier references from the AST — the CLEAN arm.
claims.why: The function parses source into an AST and extracts Name and Attribute nodes, which correspond to identifier references.

claims.text: THE ARTEFACT THIS EXISTS TO REMOVE. The first run of this module reported 10/12 detected, and every single detection contained the tokens SEEDED and DEFECT — the marker words the corpus writes into its own replacement comments. graph.identifiers scans raw source, so comments are tokens, and the measurement was detecting the LABEL rather than the defect. That is the same self-prediction artefact eval/ceiling.py separates with its clean and leaky arms, and it is why both arms are reported here.
claims.why: The claim refers to past run results and to graph.identifiers and eval/ceiling.py, none of which are in this chunk.

claims.text: Comments do not exist in an AST, and docstrings are skipped explicitly, so what remains is names the program actually uses.
claims.why: The function uses ast.parse, which excludes comments; it explicitly skips the first statement if it is a string constant (docstring).

claims.text: MULTISET, not a set. Set semantics erase the deletion of a call that still occurs elsewhere in the same function -- and "this function now calls _verify_reachable once instead of twice" is exactly the kind of change a seeded defect makes. Counting is independently correct, not a tune to the answer: it was wrong before the result was known.
claims.why: The function uses Counter to count occurrences and then flattens with multiplicity (#i), preserving multiplicity in the returned set.

claims.text: Constant VALUES per function — the layer that closes the data-only blind spot.
claims.why: The function extracts ast.Constant values per function, which captures data literals.

claims.text: Three of the five mutations the reference layer missed change no name at all: FREE_LANES gains "claude_cli"; a host constant gains localhost; an argv list loses --no-textconv. A name-based view is structurally blind to every one of them, because the identifiers are identical before and after.
claims.why: The specific mutations are not in this chunk; the claim about the reference layer is unverifiable here.

claims.text: Constants are a multiset per function, like references, so losing one of two identical flags is visible. Values are stored as repr and CLIPPED: this layer must never become a way for a secret in a literal to travel into a report.
claims.why: The function uses Counter per function and clips repr strings to 80 characters.

claims.text: Constants at MODULE level too — FREE_LANES = (...) is a module assignment, so a function-scoped walk would never see it change.
claims.why: The function walks tree.body (module-level statements) and extracts constants from Assign/AnnAssign.

claims.text: All constants, function-scoped and module-scoped, as comparable keys.
claims.why: The function combines _module_literals and _literals_by_function into a single set.

claims.text: Statement SHAPE per function — the layer for the control-flow blind spot.
claims.why: The docstring says it records node types and nesting depth, which is statement shape. The implementation is not shown but the docstring is consistent with the described purpose.

claims.text: The two mutations that neither references nor literals can see change only the shape of the code: one inserts an early return, the other inverts a condition. In both, the identifier multiset and the constant multiset are byte-identical before and after, because nothing is named or valued differently — only the control flow moved.
claims.why: The specific mutations are not in this chunk; the claim about the other layers is unverifiable here.

claims.text: So this layer records node TYPES and their nesting depth, deliberately discarding every name and every value. That makes it orthogonal to the other two by construction rather than by hope: a change that renames a variable
claims.why: The docstring states the design: record types and nesting depth, discard names and values. The implementation is not shown but the claim is about the design, which is consistent with the description.

observations.what: load_mutations uses importlib to execute tools/gate_discrimination.py; if that module has side effects at import time, they will run during corpus load.

_ast_refs counts Attribute occurrences by attribute name only, not the full dotted path; two different objects with the same attribute name in the same function are indistinguishable, which could mask a change that moves an attribute access from one object to another.

_literals_by_function and _module_literals clip long literal reprs to 80 chars with an ellipsis; two different long literals sharing the first 79 chars become identical keys, potentially hiding a change between them.
_module_literals only walks top-level Assign/AnnAssign statements, missing module-level constants defined via other statements (e.g., for loop assignments).

_ast_refs does not exclude Ellipsis from reference counting because it is not a Constant, but _literals_by_function explicitly excludes it; this asymmetry could matter if a mutation introduces or removes an ellipsis.
DeltaResult.detected is based on any scoring layer moving; a layer may move for reasons unrelated to the defect (e.g., formatting changes), causing false positives.
load_mutations registers the module in sys.modules before exec, but does not remove it on success; subsequent calls with a different path could reuse a stale module.
